review_evidence: Codex self-review: chapter theme, pedagogy stages, deterministic keys, unseen passages, assessment coverage, age fit, and source independence
title: Chandrayaan
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and assessment scenes instead of copying textbook prose.

levels.title: Find the big moon-mission news
levels.focus: identify main idea and key fact
levels.teaching_goal: Separate supporting details from the main news that an Indian spacecraft completed a journey to the Moon.

guided_check.teaching_block: The main idea answers what all the important facts are about. A launch, a long space journey, and a safe lunar landing all support one mission story.
guided_check.passage: A rocket lifted an Indian spacecraft into space. After travelling far beyond Earth, the craft reached the Moon and landed safely.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence gives the main news?
options: An Indian spacecraft completed a journey to the Moon.
The rocket made a loud sound.
accepted_answers: An Indian spacecraft completed a journey to the Moon.
an Indian spacecraft completed a journey to the Moon

bridge.teaching_block: Sort headline from detail. 'The craft reached the Moon' is the headline; 'people watched a screen' is a supporting detail.
bridge.passage: Families watched the mission screen as the landing signal arrived.
bridge.prompt: What event are the families watching?

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not choose a broad fact like 'Space is large.' The main idea must name this mission and its achievement.
masterclass.passage: The control room cheers when the lander sends a safe-arrival signal from the lunar surface.

independent_check.teaching_block: Read a fresh report and state its main idea.
independent_check.passage: After months of testing, a small research craft crossed a great distance and began sending pictures from the Moon's southern region.
independent_check.prompt: What is the report mainly about?

concept_slots.description: Name a research craft or spacecraft.
Mention reaching or sending pictures from the Moon.
State the central mission achievement, not a minor detail.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Identify the main idea in an ocean mission.
transfer_check.passage: A research boat sailed for ten days, reached a remote coral reef, and lowered cameras to record sea life.
transfer_check.prompt: State the main idea and one supporting detail.

concept_slots.description: State that a research boat explored a coral reef.
Use the journey, cameras, or sea-life detail.

levels.title: Questions that lead to discovery
levels.focus: infer curiosity and give a reason
levels.teaching_goal: Infer curiosity from purposeful questions and explain how asking experts helps learning.

guided_check.teaching_block: Curiosity is shown through wanting to know more. Rani asks what a lander does, how it slows down, and why scientists choose a landing place.
guided_check.passage: Rani pauses the news and asks three questions about the spacecraft. She writes the answers in a notebook.

bridge.teaching_block: Find evidence, then name the quality. Repeated useful questions are evidence of curiosity.
bridge.passage: A child asks the science teacher why the Moon has craters.
options: asking why the Moon has craters
accepted_answers: asking why the Moon has craters
asks why the moon has craters

masterclass.teaching_block: Curiosity is not the same as already knowing. A curious learner asks because there is more to discover.
masterclass.passage: Rani says, 'I do not understand how the craft lands without a runway. Can you explain?'
masterclass.prompt: Which reason best explains her question?
options: She wants to understand something new.
She wants the lesson to stop.
accepted_answers: She wants to understand something new.
she wants to understand something new

independent_check.teaching_block: Infer curiosity in an unseen classroom moment.
independent_check.passage: During a model-rocket activity, Faiz asks why fins keep the rocket steady and then tests two fin shapes.
independent_check.prompt: How do Faiz's actions show curiosity?

concept_slots.description: Mention his question about fins.
Mention testing two shapes.
Connect these actions to learning or curiosity.

transfer_check.passage: At the garden pond, Kiara notices fewer tadpoles near the sunny edge. She asks the gardener about shade and compares both sides of the pond.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain why Kiara's approach is curious.

concept_slots.description: Mention noticing the tadpole difference.
Mention asking about shade.
Mention comparing both pond sides.
Name curiosity or investigation.

levels.title: Unlock mission words
levels.teaching_goal: Use context to understand launch, orbit, lander, and lunar in simple mission reports.

guided_check.teaching_block: A launch is the start of a spacecraft's journey from the ground. The clue 'rose from the launch pad' shows upward movement at the beginning.
guided_check.passage: Flames appeared below the rocket as it rose from the pad and began its launch.
options: the start of a space journey
the end of a school day
accepted_answers: the start of a space journey

bridge.teaching_block: Lunar means related to the Moon. Link luna or lunar with Moon whenever the sentence describes the Moon's surface.
bridge.passage: The lander photographed rocks on the lunar ground.

masterclass.teaching_block: A lander is not the whole rocket. It is the part designed to come down safely on a surface.
masterclass.passage: The spacecraft releases a smaller machine that lowers its legs and settles on the Moon.
masterclass.prompt: Which word names the smaller machine?

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the context clue in a fresh sentence.
independent_check.passage: The craft entered orbit and travelled again and again around the Moon.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same word in an Earth-science context.
transfer_check.passage: A weather satellite follows an orbit around Earth while collecting cloud pictures.
transfer_check.prompt: What does orbit mean in this sentence?

levels.title: Tell the mission in past time
levels.focus: order events and use past tense
levels.teaching_goal: Arrange launch, travel, and landing events, and use past-tense verbs to report completed mission facts.

guided_check.teaching_block: A completed mission is reported in past tense: launched, travelled, landed. Time order follows start, journey, arrival.
guided_check.passage: The craft launched from Earth, travelled through space, and landed on the Moon.
guided_check.prompt: Which verb shows the final event?

bridge.teaching_block: Match base and past forms: launch becomes launched; travel becomes travelled; land becomes landed.
bridge.passage: Today we launch a model. Yesterday we ___ it.
bridge.prompt: Which past-tense form completes the sentence?

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not mix future and past in a report about finished events. 'The craft will land yesterday' is incorrect.
masterclass.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct tense?
options: The craft will land last week.

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange the completed events and use past-tense verbs.
independent_check.passage: Words: landed on the Moon / launched from Earth / travelled through space
independent_check.prompt: Write the mission events from first to last.
accepted_answers: launched from earth, travelled through space, landed on the moon
launched from earth travelled through space landed on the moon

transfer_check.teaching_block: Report a completed journey in a different context.
transfer_check.passage: Yesterday, a rescue boat left the harbour, crossed rough water, and reached a small island.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete past-tense sentence that keeps the event order.

concept_slots.description: Mention that the boat left the harbour.
Mention crossing rough water.
Mention reaching the island.

levels.title: Write a clear mission note
levels.focus: write complete facts and a short summary
levels.teaching_goal: Combine a mission's purpose, sequence, and result into two or three accurate sentences in the learner's own words.

guided_check.teaching_block: A fact note uses complete sentences and keeps only key information. Worked example: 'The mission carried a lander towards the Moon. It landed safely and began studying the surface.'
guided_check.passage: Purpose: study the Moon. Result: the lander reached the surface and sent information.
guided_check.prompt: Which note includes both purpose and result?
options: The mission studied the Moon after its lander reached the surface.
accepted_answers: The mission studied the Moon after its lander reached the surface.
the mission studied the Moon after its lander reached the surface

bridge.teaching_block: Build the summary from three parts: what travelled, where it went, and what it achieved.
bridge.passage: What: spacecraft. Where: Moon. Achievement: safe landing.
bridge.prompt: Which sentence contains all three parts?
options: The spacecraft reached the Moon and landed safely.
accepted_answers: The spacecraft reached the Moon and landed safely.
the spacecraft reached the Moon and landed safely

masterclass.teaching_block: Avoid copying a list of dates or machine parts. A summary connects the purpose and result in your own words.
masterclass.passage: The craft launched, travelled to the Moon, landed, and sent surface readings.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer is a useful summary?
options: A Moon mission completed its journey and began collecting information from the surface.
accepted_answers: A Moon mission completed its journey and began collecting information from the surface.
a moon mission completed its journey and began collecting information from the surface

independent_check.teaching_block: Summarize an unseen mission report without a model answer.
independent_check.passage: A small rover rolled away from its lander, photographed nearby rocks, and sent the pictures to scientists on Earth.
independent_check.prompt: Write two sentences explaining what the rover did and why the pictures mattered.

concept_slots.description: Mention that the rover moved or photographed rocks.
Mention sending pictures to Earth or scientists.
Explain that scientists could study or learn about the Moon.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Write a short information note about a different exploration tool.
transfer_check.passage: An underwater robot moved along the sea floor, recorded a coral reef, and returned video for marine scientists.
transfer_check.prompt: Write two sentences summarizing its journey and result.

concept_slots.description: Mention movement along the sea floor.
Mention recording coral or video.
Mention scientists receiving or studying the video.

items.passage: The control screen shows a green signal after the lander touches the lunar ground.
items.prompt: What does the green signal follow?

items.passage: A rover leaves the lander and takes pictures beside a shallow crater.
items.prompt: What machine takes the pictures?

items.passage: A craft travelled to an asteroid, collected a small sample, and carried it back for study.
items.prompt: Which main idea fits the report?
options: A space mission returned an asteroid sample for study.
accepted_answers: A space mission returned an asteroid sample for study.
a space mission returned an asteroid sample for study

items.passage: A balloon rose high above storms and measured temperature, wind, and moisture before returning.
items.prompt: State the main idea of the report.

concept_slots.description: Name the balloon.
Mention measuring weather conditions.
State the purpose of gathering weather information.

items.passage: Zoya asks the museum guide why a capsule needs a heat shield and sketches the answer.
items.prompt: What quality does Zoya show?

items.passage: Naman compares two paper rockets after asking which fin shape flies straighter.
items.prompt: Explain how his actions show investigation.

concept_slots.description: Mention his fin-shape question.
Mention comparing two rockets.
Explain that he wants evidence or an answer.

items.passage: Scientists test the lander's legs many times before launch.
items.prompt: Which sentence gives the clearest reason?
options: They test the legs because the lander must touch down safely.
accepted_answers: They test the legs because the lander must touch down safely.
they test the legs because the lander must touch down safely

items.passage: A rover carries a camera into a place where people cannot walk safely.
items.prompt: Explain why the camera is useful.

concept_slots.description: Mention the unsafe or hard-to-reach place.
Mention the rover taking or sending pictures.
Explain that people can observe or study remotely.

items.passage: The rocket began its ascent and climbed away from the ground.
items.prompt: What does ascent mean?

items.passage: The rover transmitted pictures, sending them by signal to Earth.
items.prompt: What does transmitted mean?

items.passage: A machine is designed to settle safely on another world's surface.
items.prompt: Which mission word names it?

items.passage: A craft follows a repeated path around Mars.
items.prompt: Write the word for this path.

items.passage: A probe launched, travelled for months, and entered orbit.
items.prompt: Which event happened first?

items.passage: Words: sent pictures / reached the planet / left Earth
items.prompt: Arrange the completed events.
accepted_answers: left earth, reached the planet, sent pictures
left earth reached the planet sent pictures

items.passage: The mission ended yesterday.
items.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct past tense?

items.passage: Last month, engineers ___ the rover wheels on rough ground.
items.prompt: Write the past form of test.

items.passage: The rover sends rock pictures to Earth.
items.prompt: Which option is a complete factual sentence?
options: The rover sends pictures of rocks to Earth.
accepted_answers: The rover sends pictures of rocks to Earth.
the rover sends pictures of rocks to earth

items.passage: A radio antenna receives the craft's signal.
items.prompt: Write one complete fact about the antenna.

concept_slots.description: Name the antenna.
Use a complete action.
Mention the craft or signal.

items.passage: A probe flew past a comet, photographed its icy surface, and sent the images home.
items.prompt: Which summary keeps the journey and result?
options: The probe visited a comet and returned useful pictures.
accepted_answers: The probe visited a comet and returned useful pictures.
the probe visited a comet and returned useful pictures

items.passage: A solar telescope opened in space, observed the Sun for a month, and sent temperature maps to researchers.
items.prompt: Summarize the tool's work in two sentences.

concept_slots.description: Name the solar telescope.
Mention observing the Sun.
Mention sending maps or helping researchers.
